questions.q: What distinguishes an audit log from a general debug log?
options: Audit logs are stored in plaintext, debug logs are encrypted
An audit log records which identity performed which operation, on which resource, and when
Audit logs only exist in on-premises systems, not the cloud
There is no real difference
questions.explain: An audit log is specifically disciplined around who, what, and when — identity, operation, resource, and timestamp — rather than general debugging detail.

questions.q: What does Azure's Activity Log capture?
options: Application-level print statements from running code
Subscription-level operations such as creating a resource or changing a role assignment
Only failed login attempts
CPU and memory metrics for virtual machines
questions.explain: The Activity Log is a feed of subscription-level events tracking operations performed against Azure resources, generated automatically with no setup required.

questions.q: Why isn't Azure's default 90-day Activity Log retention enough for most compliance needs?
options: 90 days is actually more than any compliance standard requires
Most compliance obligations, including PCI-DSS, expect audit history retained much longer than 90 days
The Activity Log doesn't work until a diagnostic setting is configured
90-day retention only applies to virtual machines
questions.explain: PCI-DSS and similar frameworks typically expect at least a year of retained audit history, far beyond Azure's automatic 90-day default — a diagnostic setting forwarding logs to a longer-retention destination closes that gap.

questions.q: Why must forwarded audit logs be tamper-resistant (write-once or access-restricted)?
options: To reduce storage costs
Because a log that can be quietly edited after the fact isn't credible evidence of anything
Because Azure requires it for all storage accounts
To make the logs load faster in the portal
questions.explain: The entire value of an audit log as evidence depends on it being a trustworthy, unaltered record. If it can be edited after the fact, it can no longer prove what actually happened.

questions.q: How does audit logging connect to PCI-DSS Requirement 10 at Northbridge Retail?
options: It doesn't — Requirement 10 is only about encryption
Requirement 10 requires tracking and monitoring access to cardholder data and related systems, which audit logging directly provides
Requirement 10 only applies to physical security
Audit logs are optional under PCI-DSS
questions.explain: PCI-DSS Requirement 10 specifically requires tracking and monitoring all access to cardholder data and the systems that touch it — audit logs retained with adequate history are the direct evidence of that.
